positioning: The creature of the mist. A long-haired Russian Blue with a silver shimmer.
story: The Nebelung is the longhaired Russian Blue, and its name means creature of the mist in German. The breed began in Denver in 1984, when a breeder named Cora Cobb mated a black shorthaired cat named Siegfried with a blue-gray longhaired cat named Brunhilde. The kittens were blue and longhaired, and she kept them.

The look is a soft shimmer. The coat is a silvery blue, with each hair tipped in silver, and the semi-long fur forms a ruff at the neck, britches on the hind legs and a plumed tail. In motion it ripples, and in the light it glints like frost.

The eyes are a clear, vivid green. A Nebelung is a fine-boned cat, long and slender, with a wedge-shaped head and a gentle, sweet expression. Like the Russian Blue it has a calm, quiet air that suits the name.

The personality is shy and devoted. A Nebelung bonds deeply with its family and may hide from strangers or loud noises, and it likes a quiet home and a routine. It is gentle, intelligent and sensitive, and it often follows one person from room to room.

Nebelungs are playful and athletic. They like to climb, chase and investigate, and they enjoy a game of fetch or a puzzle toy. They are not demanding, and they adapt well to a calm household with a stable routine and a window to watch.

The coat is easy, a weekly comb is enough. The breed is generally healthy and long-lived, but it is rare, so ask breeders about heart and genetic screening. Many Nebelungs live well into their late teens. Give it a calm home, a perch and a friend.

days: Nebelung means creature of the mist in German.
In 1984 a Denver breeder paired a black cat named Siegfried with a blue cat named Brunhilde.
A shimmering silver coat that ripples as it walks.
It vanishes when the doorbell rings and reappears when the visitor leaves.
A quiet presence can fill a room.
Ask who has seen a cat that looks like a cloud with eyes.
A silvery weight against your side, and the night is calm.
last_walk:
Blue hour on the lawn, and a light mist is rising off the grass.
The Nebelung has hidden, appeared and followed you all week. Now it sits in the mist, silver coat glinting, green eyes bright, and watches the evening go dark. One more look at the world, then home.
